scope_note: Daily edition from matching Monday /new listings: 102 non-replacement cs.CV rows, 40 cs.RO rows, 132 deduplicated papers, and 112 ROI papers. Tier A cards use official arXiv abstract pages; official arXiv HTML was available for AtlasVLA, PSG-JEPA, AutoIntervene, TEMPO, planning-token pruning, and the accessibility-field paper.
executive_thesis: The August 10 batch is about making robot policies accountable to persistent state rather than plausible next frames or smooth action chunks. AtlasVLA adds world-ego memory to VLA control, PSG-JEPA asks whether latent prediction carries physical state, AutoIntervene turns action support into a deployment switch, WNM-3D routes 3D scene context into VLN, and distractor-augmented VPR shows that a retrieval score can reward the wrong variable. APRL should turn these papers into a state-to-action audit: memory, geometry, intervention, and compression are useful only when they change a robot decision under stress.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Persistent state is now a control variable
decision_cards.body: AtlasVLA and WNM-3D both reject single-frame reactivity: the useful question is whether a world or navigation memory changes the next action when evidence leaves view.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: World models need physical probes
decision_cards.body: PSG-JEPA and TaskSense imply that forward prediction and reconstruction are weak objectives unless the latent can expose proprioceptive state or task-relevant regions.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Evaluation must attack shortcut variables
decision_cards.body: VPR distractors, intervention thresholds, viewpoint shifts, and planning-token pruning all ask whether the measured success is attached to identity, state, or only conditions.

papers.title: AtlasVLA: Persistent World-Ego State Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.fit: VLA execution memory - world state - ego task progress
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML checked
papers.status_quo: Many VLA policies remain reactive, conditioning the next action on the current observation and instruction.
papers.friction: A wrist-camera robot loses objects outside the field of view and loses task progress during long-horizon execution.
papers.hidden_premise: A persistent spatial memory and an ego-progress memory can be made action-relevant without requiring multiple live cameras.
papers.conceptual_move: Lift transient wrist observations into a voxel-hashed 4D world state and pair it with an ego-working state memory for the policy.
papers.mechanism: The abstract reports a dual-memory architecture that conditions a diffusion transformer on persistent world-ego state.

evidence.claim: The paper names perception forgetting and temporal task-progress forgetting as the bottlenecks.
It claims a 4D Persistent World State Memory plus Ego-Working State Memory improves LIBERO, RLBench, and real-world manipulation.
APRL should test memory usefulness by removing objects from view and measuring action changes before final failure.

papers.falsification: If the persistent state does not improve recovery after occlusion, viewpoint change, or multi-step interruption, it is only an expensive context cache.
papers.adversarial: Memory can hide benchmark priors, so success should be split by object exit, revisit, phase boundary, and recovery segment.
papers.thinking_tool: Treat memory as a hypothesis about hidden task state, not as an extra perception feature.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for manipulation and long-horizon tasks; weaker for purely reactive contact servoing where the state is fully observed.

papers.title: Is Forward Prediction Enough? Physical State Grounding for JEPA World Models
papers.fit: world model - latent grounding - proprioceptive state
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML checked
papers.status_quo: JEPA-style world models often optimize action-conditioned latent prediction rather than explicit robot-state identifiability.
papers.friction: A latent can predict the next embedding while failing to expose joint state or state change needed by a planner.
papers.hidden_premise: A useful world model should make physical state readable from individual latents and multi-horizon state change readable from latent pairs.
papers.conceptual_move: Add proprioceptive-state and joint-angle-change grounding losses during training while keeping inference cost unchanged.
papers.mechanism: The abstract states that PSG-JEPA adds two grounding objectives and evaluates probing, frozen-latent planning, and policy learning.

evidence.claim: The paper directly asks whether forward prediction alone enforces reliable physical-state identifiability.
It evaluates latent identifiability, goal-conditioned planning, simulation policy learning, and real-robot policy learning.
APRL should require a frozen-latent physical-state probe before trusting a world model for control.

papers.falsification: If latent probes improve while planning and policy learning do not, physical grounding is diagnostic but not operational.
papers.adversarial: Proprioceptive probes may overfit robot morphology, so cross-object and cross-task transfer should be separated.
papers.thinking_tool: Ask whether the world model latent contains the state variable the controller will actually use.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for robot world models and model-based control; less direct for video-only generation without action consumption.

papers.title: AutoIntervene: Calibrated Intervention for Action-Chunking Imitation Learning Policies
papers.fit: deployment intervention - action support memory - operator handoff
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML checked
papers.status_quo: Action-chunking policies can keep producing smooth chunks after perception or execution drift leaves the demonstration distribution.
papers.friction: Smoothness can mask state inconsistency, so the system needs a calibrated handoff before damage accumulates.
papers.hidden_premise: Support should be measured jointly in visual state and proposed action space, with separate thresholds for taking and returning control.
papers.conceptual_move: Compare proposed chunks against a visual-action support memory from successful executions and use quantile-calibrated transfer thresholds.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes phase-local support for policy-to-operator transfer and global support for operator-to-policy return.

evidence.claim: The paper names perception errors and execution drift as failure modes for action chunks.
It calibrates separate switching thresholds from held-out expert demonstration score quantiles.
APRL should log intervention segments as training data only when they cover learner-induced states.

papers.falsification: If support scores do not predict recoverable failure earlier than task failure, intervention is reactive teleoperation rather than policy governance.
papers.adversarial: Operator return can bias the learner toward easy recovery states unless phase labels and failed interventions are retained.
papers.thinking_tool: Measure whether confidence changes the controller authority, not only whether it correlates with success.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for action-chunking imitation policies; less direct for policies without operator recovery or chunked action output.

papers.title: WNM-3D: A World Navigation Model with 3D Scene Conditioning for Closed-Loop VLN
papers.fit: vision-language navigation - 3D scene prefix - world-action diffusion
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract checked; official /html returned 404 during this run
papers.status_quo: VLN systems increasingly adapt VLMs into action policies without explicitly modeling how observations should evolve under motion.
papers.friction: Action-centric training can follow language while ignoring geometry that determines which future view should appear after movement.
papers.hidden_premise: A frozen geometry encoder can consolidate egocentric RGB history into a 3D scene prefix that conditions future video-action blocks.
papers.conceptual_move: Feed geometry-aware tokens into a world-action diffusion transformer through block-causal attention for closed-loop VLN.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes monocular history, a 3D Scene-to-Token Adapter, and joint future-view/action generation.

evidence.claim: The paper argues existing WAMs for continuous VLN lack geometry-aware conditioning from observed history.
It proposes a fixed-length 3D scene prefix that conditions every future video-action block.
APRL should score whether geometry prefix errors predict wrong turns before navigation failure.

papers.falsification: If 3D scene conditioning does not outperform history-only tokens under layout ambiguity, the geometry path is decorative.
papers.adversarial: A frozen geometry encoder can import reconstruction biases that look like navigation competence in static scenes.
papers.thinking_tool: Tie every map token to an action or future-view prediction it changes.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for VLN and object navigation; weaker for manipulation unless scene geometry maps to reachable contacts.

papers.title: TEMPO: Semantic-Action Decoupled RL Post-Training for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.fit: VLA post-training - semantic/action decoupling - two-timescale RL
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML checked
papers.status_quo: VLA post-training often applies one update strategy across semantic representations and low-level action modules.
papers.friction: Fast online RL updates can destabilize pretrained semantic features even when only the action expert needs rapid adaptation.
papers.hidden_premise: Semantic projection and action expert should be optimized at different rates because they serve different control roles.
papers.conceptual_move: Freeze the vision-language backbone and use two dedicated RL loops: slow semantic projection updates and fast action expert updates.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes semantic-action decoupling, two-timescale RL, CALVIN evaluation, and real-world manipulation tasks.

evidence.claim: The paper identifies distribution mismatch in SFT and uniform RL updates as the post-training problem.
It updates semantic projection infrequently and the action expert frequently to preserve semantic stability.
APRL should monitor semantic drift and action improvement as separate curves during RL post-training.

papers.falsification: If semantic drift is not lower than uniform RL at equal success, the decoupling does not solve the stated failure.
papers.adversarial: Freezing the backbone can preserve a wrong semantic prior, so failures need object and instruction-level attribution.
papers.thinking_tool: Separate what the robot understands from how it converts that understanding into motor correction.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for VLA manipulation post-training; less direct for modular planners whose semantic and action modules are already separate.

papers.title: Depth-Wise Probing and Pruning of the Planning Token in a Driving Vision-Language-Action Model
papers.fit: driving VLA - planning token - depth pruning
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML checked
papers.status_quo: A driving VLA may route trajectory planning through the full depth of a language model even when the action signal appears early.
papers.friction: Semantic intent can be linearly readable before the planning token is in the format expected by the deployed planner.
papers.hidden_premise: Planner compatibility and semantic decodability are different signals and should be measured layer by layer.
papers.conceptual_move: Use a trajectory-space logit lens to decode the planning token across 32 decoder layers and prune by angular deviation.
papers.mechanism: The abstract reports early command decodability, gradual planner compatibility improvement, learned readouts, and layer ranking for pruning.

evidence.claim: Command-probe accuracy reaches 97.7 percent after the first decoder layer, while native planner compatibility improves across depth.
The paper ranks decoder layers by angular deviation induced in the planning token.
APRL should distinguish intention availability from controller-usable action format.

papers.falsification: If pruned layers fail under closed-loop perturbations despite open-loop compatibility, the token diagnostic misses feedback sensitivity.
papers.adversarial: Open-loop Avg-L2 can hide rare safety-critical maneuvers, so pruning needs scenario-level failure stratification.
papers.thinking_tool: Do not ask whether an LLM knows the command; ask when the action representation becomes executable.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for token-based VLA planners; less direct for continuous policies without a discrete planning bottleneck.

papers.title: Are Visual Place Recognition Models Recognizing Places or Conditions? Distractor-Augmented Evaluation and Condition Suppression
papers.fit: place recognition - distractor evaluation - condition suppression
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract checked; official /html returned 404 during this run
papers.status_quo: Long-term VPR is usually judged by Recall@1 between one query condition and another database condition.
papers.friction: Crowdsourced map databases can contain distractors that match illumination, weather, or season while depicting the wrong place.
papers.hidden_premise: A descriptor can be discriminative by encoding condition information, which is useful for matching but harmful for place identity.
papers.conceptual_move: Introduce Distractor-Augmented Recall and suppress condition information with INLP and LEACE.
papers.mechanism: The abstract reports ranking reversals under DAR@1 and improvement after condition suppression without reducing standard R@1.

evidence.claim: The paper says method rankings under DAR@1 differ from standard Recall@1.
It reports that condition suppression can improve distractor robustness without reducing R@1.
APRL should apply condition distractors to localization and map retrieval before claiming place robustness.

papers.falsification: If condition suppression hurts loop-closure precision in mixed real maps, the method trades one shortcut for another.
papers.adversarial: A suppression method can remove condition evidence that is genuinely needed for localization under appearance change.
papers.thinking_tool: Attack the nuisance variable that the benchmark quietly rewards.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for place recognition and loop closure; less direct for semantic mapping without retrieval decisions.

papers.title: Beyond Visibility: Real-Time Surface Accessibility Fields from Sparse LiDAR
papers.fit: robot geometry - surface accessibility - sparse LiDAR
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML checked
papers.status_quo: 3D perception often stops at visibility or reconstruction, leaving tool-specific physical access to later planning heuristics.
papers.friction: Complete meshes and fixed bases are unrealistic for mobile robots mapping from sparse streaming LiDAR.
papers.hidden_premise: Accessibility can be represented as a per-point field conditioned on the tool and approach corridor, updated at sensor rate.
papers.conceptual_move: Evaluate each surface point against rotated tool-geometry kernels and approach-corridor clearance on a scan-centric TSDF.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes a GPU accessibility field from sparse LiDAR, collision kernels, and sensor-rate updates.

evidence.claim: The paper distinguishes physical surface accessibility from visibility estimation.
It checks tool collisions and approach-corridor clearance from streaming sparse LiDAR.
APRL should evaluate geometry by reachable-contact success rather than map completeness alone.

papers.falsification: If accessibility labels do not predict successful approach and contact under sensor sparsity, the field is not robot-usable.
papers.adversarial: Tool kernels can encode a narrow gripper model, so transfer to different end effectors needs explicit tests.
papers.thinking_tool: A map is valuable when it names what the robot can physically do next.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for mobile manipulation and inspection; less direct for scene understanding tasks without tool geometry.

synthesis.title: Memory and world models converge on state identifiability
synthesis.facts: The papers separately add persistent world-ego state, physical grounding losses, and 3D scene prefixes.
synthesis.inference: The common decision is whether hidden state can be recovered early enough to change action choice.

synthesis.title: Control authority becomes a measured switch
synthesis.facts: One paper transfers authority to an operator, one separates semantic/action RL rates, and one probes when a planning token becomes executable.
synthesis.inference: APRL should instrument controller authority, semantic drift, and action-format readiness as separate deployment signals.

synthesis.title: Geometry is useful when it resists shortcut evaluation
synthesis.facts: The batch tests whether descriptors encode conditions, surfaces are physically accessible, and navigation uses 3D scene history.
synthesis.inference: Map and retrieval benchmarks should include nuisance-variable distractors and contact/navigation consequences.

frontier_memory.label: Strengthening
frontier_memory.body: August 10 strengthens the same axis by making persistent state, intervention thresholds, and planning-token readiness explicit.

frontier_memory.label: New signal
frontier_memory.history: Recent WAM notes focused on future prediction and physical fidelity.
frontier_memory.body: PSG-JEPA asks for physical-state identifiability inside the latent, not only better rollout quality.

frontier_memory.label: Missing axis
frontier_memory.history: Late July and early August geometry notes focused on maps, SLAM, and reconstruction.
frontier_memory.body: Accessibility fields and VPR distractors add action reachability and nuisance-variable suppression as missing evaluation axes.

strategy.title: Persistent-state VLA failure audit
strategy.thesis: Measure whether world-ego memory, semantic-action decoupling, and action-support thresholds predict failure before the robot loses recoverability.
strategy.one_week: Replay one LIBERO-style task with object exit, camera shift, and phase interruption while logging memory state, support score, and action deltas.
strategy.four_week: Build a benchmark that compares reactive VLA, persistent-memory VLA, and intervention-gated VLA under the same recoverability labels.
strategy.success: At least two state signals predict different failure families earlier than task-level failure.
strategy.stop: Memory and support scores collapse to generic confidence and do not change recovery ranking.
strategy.asset: Occlusion/interruption rollouts, state-memory dumps, intervention labels, and action-delta traces.

strategy.title: Physical-state world-model probe suite
strategy.thesis: Require latent world models to expose proprioceptive state, state changes, and task-relevant visual regions before using them for planning.
strategy.one_week: Add frozen-latent probes for joint state and state change to one existing robot world-model dataset.
strategy.four_week: Compare forward-prediction-only, physical-grounded, and task-attended world models on planning and real-robot transfer.
strategy.success: Probe quality explains planning improvement better than reconstruction loss or visual rollout quality.
strategy.stop: Physical probes improve but downstream planning and policy learning remain unchanged.
strategy.asset: Latent probe scripts, robot-state labels, task-attention masks, and planning success logs.

strategy.title: Robot-usable geometry and shortcut evaluation
strategy.thesis: Turn maps and descriptors into action-facing tests: accessibility, loop-closure distractors, and 3D navigation tokens must change robot decisions.
strategy.one_week: Create a small testbed with condition distractors, sparse LiDAR surfaces, and tool-specific approach constraints.
strategy.four_week: Evaluate VPR, semantic mapping, and accessibility-field methods by navigation/contact success rather than standalone map quality.
strategy.success: The benchmark changes method ranking relative to standard retrieval or reconstruction metrics.
strategy.stop: Action-facing metrics track standard metrics so closely that the new labels add no decision value.
strategy.asset: Distractor maps, accessibility labels, tool kernels, and closed-loop navigation/contact traces.
